body: Drakan: The Ancients' Gates is Surreal Software's PlayStation 2 action-adventure, first released in North America on 29 January 2002. Rynn and the dragon Arokh continue the partnership introduced in Drakan: Order of the Flame, travelling through a fantasy world on foot and in the air. The two scales give the adventure its shape. A fortress can be a place to approach through its doors or a landmark seen from above. The player moves between Rynn's immediate struggle with enemies and the wider freedom offered by a dragon in flight.

Rynn uses weapons and magic during the on-foot sections, with a target lock helping keep attention on a particular enemy. Spells are performed through directional inputs, making their use another activity to learn alongside movement and attacks. Shops and discoveries provide equipment for later encounters. Arokh changes the pace through flight and aerial combat, opening routes that belong to a different scale of the landscape. Returning to the ground makes those large spaces tangible again, connecting the view from the sky to the passages and opponents waiting below.

The original Drakan appeared on Windows in 1999, while The Ancients' Gates continued the world exclusively on PlayStation 2. Alan Patmore led the design, with Erik Aho composing its music. The sequel retained the partnership at the centre of the earlier game while expanding Rynn's equipment and magical abilities. PAL editions followed in July 2002. Its distinctive pleasure is the connection between the two protagonists: the dragon is more than a distant story companion because flying with Arokh becomes a regular way of inhabiting the same world Rynn explores on foot.
